sn8.1:1.2: This chapter features the poetry of Vaṅgīsa, the finest poet of the Sangha. These discourses provide a prose setting for his Theragāthā verses at [thag21.1](); there are notable differences between the two versions. In several passages, including this one, he reflects on the struggles he faced in his path, showing a high degree of self-awareness and persistence.
sn8.1:1.4: Period art depicts women as bare-breasted and draped in elaborate jewellery.
sn8.1:1.5: “Dissatisfaction” (_anabhirati_) with his life of seclusion and celibacy.
sn8.1:3.1: There is some confusion regarding the Pali _ugga_ (“warrior chief”). Both Pali commentaries and Sanskrit sources (Manu 10.9) know of a caste called _ugga_ (Sanskrit _ugra_) born of a _khattiya_ father and a _sudda_ mother. This was a caste reviled as cruel, whose duty was catching snakes and other underground vermin (Manu 10.49). This is completely different from the aristocratic warriors referred to here. The distinction is noted in Medhātithi’s commentary to Manu 4.212, who says the Vedic _ugra_ was a key figure in the king’s alliance, which is supported by the use at [dn3:2.7.2]().
